claims.claim: mark (or drop) traffic at the virtual port so the physical network can prioritise it, without relying on guests.
Distributed port group (or an uplink port group) -> Configure -> Traffic filtering and marking -> Enable, then add rules.
Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins.
voice EF (46), video AF41 (34), vMotion CS1 (8, scavenger), storage AF31 (26).
**Direction**: ingress (into the switch from the VM), egress, or both.
system traffic type (vMotion, vSAN, NFS, management, iSCSI, VM), MAC (src/dst/VLAN/EtherType), IP (protocol, ports, addresses).
Rule "voice-ef": Tag, DSCP 46, CoS 5, ingress, qualifier IP protocol UDP dst ports 16384-32767.
On the uplink port group: Tag DSCP 8, qualifier system traffic = vMotion, egress.
DSCP set here overwrites the guest marking; to trust the guest, do not add a Tag rule for that traffic.
CoS only travels on tagged frames (VLAN trunk); on access ports it is lost.
Drop rules are a coarse firewall without logging; use NSX or the guest firewall for real policy.
vDS 5.5+ is required; standard switches have no marking.
shows the expected `tos 0xb8` (DSCP 46) on egress frames; switch QoS counters increment in the right queue.

coverage: I extracted every concrete claim in the skill — the client navigation path, the full rule anatomy (actions, CoS and DSCP ranges with the example EF/AF41/CS1/AF31 values, directions, all three qualifier classes), both worked examples with their DSCP/CoS values and the 16384-32767 UDP port range, every gotcha including the vDS 5.5+ version statement, and the whole pktcap-uw/tcpdump-uw verify command with its expected tos 0xb8 — and checked each against the skill's only listed source.
suggested_edits: The only listed source is the vSphere 8.0 documentation library landing page, which is a table of contents and states none of the skill's facts, so every claim is unverifiable as sourced. The content actually lives in the vSphere Networking book's policies chapter; list the deep pages instead, e.g. https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vsphere/vsphere/8-0/vsphere-networking/networking-policies/traffic-filtering-policy.html (what is traffic filtering and marking policy), .../traffic-filtering-policy/traffic-filtering-and-marking-for-a-group.html and its sub-pages (enable/mark/filter/network traffic rules, where the Allow/Drop/Tag actions, CoS/DSCP tagging and the Configure tab path are described), .../traffic-filtering-policy/qualifying-traffic-for-filtering-and-marking.html and its system/MAC/IP qualifier sub-pages, plus https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vsphere/vsphere/8-0/vsphere-networking/monitoring-network-packets.html for the pktcap-uw verification step. While re-verifying, also check the gotchas: the what-is page states the policy does not support vSphere distributed switches configured with network offloads compatibility (a missing gotcha), the DiffServ conventions EF 46/AF41 34/CS1 8/AF31 26 and the RTP port range 16384-32767 are generic networking facts that vSphere docs do not state and need their own sources (RFC/Cisco), and 'first match wins' should be reconciled with the documented ordered rule set with modifiable rule priorities.
